nodes.speaker: The Scissor-Man
nodes.text: ...That isn't how it works. You can't just put it back.

[i]The clippings are all around him now, hundreds of them, small cut-out scenes with their edges still sharp. In one, a young man hammers a blade straight and then does not. In another, a boy tears out a page. In another, a woman sets a table for six, and then for one.[/i]

nodes.speaker: The Scissor-Man
nodes.text: I cut them to keep the story short. Every one of them was somebody's favorite part.
[i]You hold up the lantern. In its light the clippings turn over, one at a time. Every one has a back side, and on every back side something has been written: kept.[/i]
[i]The shears fall open and are only shears. Without them his hands are just hands: a tailor's, thimble-dented and tired.[/i]

nodes.speaker: Wick
nodes.text: My name's Wick. I used to mend things. Somewhere along the way I got confused and started cutting them out instead.

nodes.speaker: Wick
nodes.text: Take this. It's the only thing I ever made that I didn't have to cut anything off to finish.
